name: Honduras Organic 18 Rabbit Yellow Honey
vendor_notes: Mild floral notes, very sweet, creamy body with honeysuckle. Brightness 6/7, sweetness 6/7, body 1/7. CoE top-10 finalist farm.
goal: Sweet, bright, floral light roast for espresso with some body
rationale: Lower altitude (1,400 m) Catuai is less dense than the Ethiopian, and honey processing leaves fruit sugars on the bean. It browns faster and can scorch or tip if the start is too hot, so it charges cooler (185 C) with a gentler burner. Body is listed as very light (1/7), which makes thin espresso, so this plan gives it a little more Maillard time and development (DTR ~19%, ~11 C after FC) to build sweetness and body without losing the honeysuckle. Honey coffees have more chaff and smoke, so air comes up a bit earlier.
steps: Preheat to 185 C, then hold steady 10+ min (BT/ET flat).
Charge 170 g at BT 185. Burner 70%, air 30, drum 90.
TP ~0:36 near 110 C. RoR is highest here, then falls.
At 178 C (~6:09): burner 45%. RoR ~10 and falling.
FC ~7:15 at ~188 C: burner 40%, air 55. Then 35%.
Drop ~8:55 at ~198.5 C (10.5 C after FC).

rest.note: Light honey coffee: too fresh it is gassy and sharp. The honeysuckle sweetness opens up from about day 8.

history.note: Initial plan from vendor data (Coffee Bean Corral) and Kaleido M1 behaviour. FC temperature is a guess until your first roast calibrates the probe.

Roast 1 (2026-09-29): short preheat, charged while climbing at 100% burner, TP 0:38 and +24 C ahead by 1:40; mid-roast recovered, but burner went back up to 60% and RoR rose to 14.5 at FC, forcing an early drop (DTR 13.7%). FC measured 188.9 C. v2: TP 0:42 to match this drum, FC 188, drop 198.5, charge burner 70%, steady preheat, and burner steps start ~2 min before FC.

Re-fitted the first 3-4 minutes to five real roasts (2026-09-29 to 10-02): on this roaster TP comes at ~0:35 at 108-116 C (not ~0:42 at ~100 C), RoR is highest right after TP and only falls, dry end lands ~3:35-3:55 and FC ~7:12-7:25 at 187-189 C. Earlier versions put the start 10-20 C too low, which invited cutting heat early and a hot finish. FC temperature, roast level and development are unchanged.
